content.title: About
content.content: Sirloin beef steak is a lean cut taken from the back of the cow. It offers a tender flavor, moderate fat content, and a satisfying texture. The NS (no‑salt) version is unseasoned, allowing the natural taste of the meat to shine.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Sirloin is one of the most popular cuts for steaks because of its balance of tenderness and flavor.
Beef provides all essential amino acids required by humans.
Traditionally, sirloin is grilled, pan‑seared, or roasted at high heat.
Its fat content is generally lower than ribeye or New York strip.
The cut is known as “sirloin” in the US and UK, and often called “вырезка” in Russian.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: A 100 g serving delivers about 26 g of high‑quality protein, essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Contains iron and zinc
items.content: Beef is a good source of heme iron, which is highly bioavailable, and zinc, which supports immune function.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Sirloin is abundant in vitamin B12, niacin (B3), and riboflavin (B2), all important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Low in added fat
items.content: The NS version has minimal added fat, making it suitable for calorie‑controlled diets.

items.title: Supports muscle mass
items.content: High protein and amino acid content help maintain and build muscle, especially with regular exercise.

items.title: Foodborne illness
items.content: Undercooked beef may harbor harmful bacteria such as E. coli. Cook steak to an internal temperature of at least 63 °C.

items.title: High purine content
items.content: Beef contains purines, which can raise uric acid levels in people prone to gout.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: Rare, but some individuals may experience an allergic reaction to beef.

items.title: Sodium in processed versions
items.content: While NS is unsalted, pre‑marinated products can add significant sodium.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Sirloin steak is best cooked over high heat—grill, cast‑iron skillet, or oven—reaching your preferred doneness (rare, medium, well‑done). Let the steak rest at room temperature for 20‑30 minutes before cooking and rest 5‑10 minutes after cooking so juices redistribute. Serve with vegetables, herbs, or a light sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep fresh steak refrigerated at 0‑4 °C for 2‑3 days. For longer storage, freeze in an airtight bag at –18 °C for up to 6 months. Thaw in the refrigerator, not at room temperature, before cooking.
